sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. for the State.
2. Learned AGA has filed counter affidavit, the same is taken on record.

3. As per learned counsel for the applicant, the present applicant is in jail since 29.9.2023 in Case Crime No.257 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act,
Police Station- Kunda, District- Pratapgarh.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that the present applicant has been falsely implicated in this case as he has not committed any offence as alleged.
5. Attention has been drawn towards the impugned F.I.R. wherein general allegations have been leveled against three accused persons including the present applicant.
Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that at the time of 'Panchnama' the family members of both sides were present wherein the allegation of demand of dowry has been made.

Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that actually this is not the case of demand of dowry or torturing the victim inasmuch as the husband of the victim (since deceased) had seen her with one more person namely, Deepak,
therefore, sudden fight started between him and Deepak where the husband of the victim (since deceased) had also sustained injuries.
The victim (since deceased) i.e. daughter-in-law of the present applicant tried to pacify the dispute wherein she got injured and resultant thereof, she died later on.

6. Learned counsel for the applicant has further submitted that the present applicant, who is father-in-law of the victim (since deceased) was having cordial relation with her and he had never demanded any dowry from her or her family members and never tortured her in the name of dowry.
As a matter of fact, he had nothing to do with the family affairs of his son and his wife.

Further,
co-accused Anara Devi, who is mother-in-law of the deceased and similar allegations have been levelled against her, has been enlarged on bail vide order dated 24.04.2024 passed by this Court in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.4493 of 2024, therefore, on the basis of principles of parity, the present applicant may also be enlarged on bail.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.4493 of 2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 7. Learned counsel for the applicant has given undertaking on behalf of the applicant that the applicant shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall cooperate in the trial proceedings and shall abide by all terms and conditions of the bail order, if granted by this Court.

8. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail by submitting that the victim (since deceased) was having four ante-mortem injuries and since she died in the house of in-laws, therefore, the present applicant, who is father-in-law cannot escape from his responsibility.

9. Without entering into merits of the case; considering the arguments of learned counsel for the parties; contents and allegations of the F.I.R.; the fact that the applicant is father-in-law of the victim (since deceased) and he was having cordial relation with her; he had never demanded any dowry from the victim or her family members and never tortured her in the name of dowry; the applicant had nothing to do with the family affairs of his son and his wife; co-accused Anara Devi having similar role has been granted bail by this Court and undertaking given on behalf of the applicant that he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall cooperate in the trial proceedings, the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
10.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

11. Let applicant- Ram Bahadur Patel be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-

sentences.text: (i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation,
then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law,
under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
(v)The applicant shall not leave India without previous permission of the court.
[Rajesh Singh Chauhan,J.]
